r1.name: MedlinePlus (U.S. National Library of Medicine, NIH)

r4.name: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health — The Nutrition Source

organs.name: Heart
functions: Pumps blood through the body (roughly 100,000 beats/day)
Delivers oxygen and nutrients to tissues
Removes carbon dioxide and metabolic waste
Helps maintain blood pressure
nutritionNeeds: Soluble fibre: part of 25–30g/day total fibre
activity: 150 min/week moderate aerobic activity, or 75 min vigorous
deterioration: Trans fats and excess saturated fat

organs.name: Lungs
functions: Gas exchange — oxygen in, carbon dioxide out
Helps regulate blood pH via CO2 removal
Filters small clots from venous blood
activity: Aerobic exercise to build lung capacity

organs.name: Liver
functions: Detoxifies blood
Produces bile for fat digestion
Stores glycogen and vitamins
Synthesises proteins including clotting factors
Metabolises medications and alcohol
activity: Regular moderate exercise to reduce fatty-liver risk
deterioration: High intake of added sugar / processed food

organs.name: Stomach
functions: Stores food temporarily
Secretes acid and pepsin to begin protein digestion
Churns food into chyme
Regulates release into the small intestine
nutritionNeeds: Vitamin B12 (needs intrinsic factor made here)

organs.name: Small Intestine
functions: Main site of nutrient digestion and absorption
Uses enzymes from the pancreas and bile from the liver
nutritionNeeds: Absorption depends on B12, folate, iron intake

organs.name: Large Intestine
functions: Absorbs water and electrolytes
Hosts the microbiome that ferments fibre
Forms and stores stool

organs.name: Pancreas
functions: Produces digestive enzymes (lipase, amylase, protease)
Produces insulin and glucagon to regulate blood glucose
activity: Regular aerobic activity improves insulin sensitivity

organs.name: Kidneys
functions: Filter blood, removing waste and excess fluid as urine
Regulate electrolyte balance
Help regulate blood pressure (via renin)
Activate vitamin D
Stimulate red blood cell production (erythropoietin)
nutritionNeeds: Moderate, not excessive, protein and sodium
deterioration: Very high protein intake in susceptible people

organs.name: Bladder
functions: Stores urine produced by the kidneys
Contracts to expel urine

organs.name: Brain
functions: Controls cognition, memory and emotion
Coordinates voluntary movement
Regulates autonomic functions (breathing, heart rate)
Processes sensory input

organs.name: Spinal Cord
functions: Relays signals between brain and body
Coordinates reflexes
Protected within the vertebral column

organs.name: Bones
functions: Structural support
Protects internal organs
Stores calcium and phosphorus
Produces blood cells (bone marrow)
activity: Sensible sunlight exposure for vitamin D
deterioration: Very high caffeine or soda intake

organs.name: Skeletal Muscles
functions: Enable voluntary movement and posture
Generate heat
Support glucose metabolism

organs.name: Thyroid
functions: Produces hormones (T3/T4) that regulate metabolism, growth and energy use
deterioration: Very high raw cruciferous-vegetable intake without adequate iodine

organs.name: Adrenal Glands
functions: Produce cortisol (stress response)
Produce adrenaline
Produce aldosterone (sodium & fluid balance)

organs.name: Skin
functions: Protective barrier against pathogens and UV
Regulates temperature via sweating
Synthesises vitamin D from sunlight
Sensory organ for touch

organs.name: Eyes
functions: Capture light and convert it to neural signals for the brain to interpret as vision

organs.name: Aorta
functions: The body's largest artery — carries oxygen-rich blood from the heart to the rest of the body

organs.name: Vena Cava (Superior & Inferior)
functions: The two largest veins — return oxygen-poor blood from the upper and lower body back to the heart

organs.name: Coronary Arteries
functions: Supply oxygen-rich blood to the heart muscle itself

organs.name: Carotid Arteries
functions: Main arteries supplying blood to the brain, neck and face

organs.name: Trachea (Windpipe)
functions: Airway connecting the throat to the bronchi, carrying air to and from the lungs

organs.name: Bronchi
functions: Branching airways carrying air from the trachea into each lung

organs.name: Diaphragm
functions: Main muscle of breathing — contracts to draw air into the lungs

organs.name: Oesophagus
functions: Muscular tube carrying swallowed food from the throat to the stomach

organs.name: Gallbladder
functions: Stores and concentrates bile made by the liver, releasing it to help digest fat

organs.name: Salivary Glands
functions: Produce saliva to begin starch digestion and ease swallowing

organs.name: Vagus Nerve
functions: Major nerve linking the brain to the heart, lungs and digestive tract; central to the rest-and-digest response

organs.name: Sciatic Nerve
functions: The body's longest nerve, running from the lower spine down each leg

organs.name: Peripheral Nerves
functions: Network of nerves carrying signals between the spinal cord and the rest of the body

organs.name: Ureters
functions: Thin tubes carrying urine from each kidney down to the bladder

organs.name: Urethra
functions: Tube carrying urine from the bladder out of the body

organs.name: Renal Blood Vessels
functions: The renal artery and vein carry blood to and from each kidney for filtering

organs.name: Vertebral Column (Spine)
functions: Chain of vertebrae protecting the spinal cord and supporting the trunk

organs.name: Ribcage
functions: Bony cage protecting the heart and lungs and assisting breathing

organs.name: Joints & Cartilage
functions: Cushion and connect bones, allowing smooth, low-friction movement

organs.name: Tendons & Ligaments
functions: Tendons attach muscle to bone; ligaments attach bone to bone, stabilising joints

organs.name: Pituitary Gland
functions: The body's "master gland" — signals the thyroid, adrenal glands and other glands to release their hormones

organs.name: Parathyroid Glands
functions: Four small glands beside the thyroid that regulate blood calcium levels

organs.name: Pineal Gland
functions: Small brain gland that produces melatonin, regulating the sleep–wake cycle

organs.name: Sweat Glands
functions: Release sweat to cool the body via evaporation

organs.name: Sebaceous Glands
functions: Produce oil (sebum) that lubricates and waterproofs the skin and hair

organs.name: Hair & Nails
functions: Protective keratin structures growing from the skin

organs.name: Ears
functions: Capture sound waves and maintain balance

organs.name: Optic Nerve
functions: Carries visual signals from each eye to the brain

organs.name: Olfactory System (Nose)
functions: Detects smell and contributes strongly to taste perception

foods.name: Fresh Outdoor Air
nutrition: Oxygen: ~21% of atmosphere, used in every cell's energy production

foods.name: Clean, Well-Ventilated Air
nutrition: Low particulate matter (PM2.5) reduces airway irritation

foods.name: Mineral Water
foods.servingQty: 1–2 cups/day, as part of total fluids
nutrition: Calcium, Magnesium and other trace minerals (source-dependent)

foods.name: Brazil Nuts
organs: Thyroid: 1–2 nuts/day — more is not better here, selenium can reach toxic levels

foods.name: Black Pepper
nutrition: Piperine — enhances absorption of some nutrients

diseases.name: Coronary Artery Disease
cause: Long-term plaque buildup (atherosclerosis) in the coronary arteries
symptoms: Chest pain or pressure (angina), often with exertion
Pain radiating to the arm, jaw or back
remedies: Diagnosis and ongoing monitoring by a cardiologist
Medication as prescribed by a physician (e.g. statins, antiplatelet or blood-pressure therapy)
Procedures such as angioplasty or bypass surgery in advanced cases
homeRemedies: Heart-healthy diet low in sodium and saturated fat
Regular moderate aerobic activity once cleared by a doctor
naturalRemedies: Garlic and omega-3-rich foods are commonly discussed as heart-supportive; check with a doctor before adding supplements alongside heart medication

diseases.name: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
symptoms: Occasionally headache, dizziness or nosebleeds at very high readings
remedies: Regular blood pressure monitoring
Medication as prescribed by a physician when lifestyle change is not enough
naturalRemedies: Potassium-rich foods (bananas, leafy greens) are commonly discussed as supportive of healthy blood pressure

diseases.name: Asthma
cause: Airway inflammation triggered by allergens, exercise, cold air or irritants
remedies: Diagnosis and a written action plan from a doctor
Prescribed inhaled medication used as directed
homeRemedies: Using a humidifier in dry conditions
naturalRemedies: Staying well hydrated and avoiding smoke exposure are commonly recommended supportive measures

diseases.name: COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease)
cause: Prolonged exposure to air pollutants or occupational dust/fumes
remedies: Diagnosis and staging by a doctor
Prescribed bronchodilators or other medication
Pulmonary rehabilitation programmes
homeRemedies: Smoking cessation — the single most effective step
naturalRemedies: Breathing techniques such as pursed-lip breathing are commonly taught alongside medical care

diseases.name: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease
cause: High intake of refined sugar and processed food
symptoms: Mild discomfort under the right ribs in later stages
remedies: Diagnosis via blood tests or imaging by a doctor
Monitoring of liver enzymes over time
homeRemedies: Reducing added sugar and refined carbohydrates
naturalRemedies: Coffee (in moderation) and a Mediterranean-style diet are commonly discussed in liver-health research

diseases.name: Gastritis
remedies: Testing for H. pylori and treatment as prescribed by a doctor if present
Reviewing NSAID or alcohol use with a physician
homeRemedies: Avoiding personal trigger foods (very spicy, fatty, or acidic, in sensitive individuals)
naturalRemedies: Ginger tea is commonly used to ease mild nausea

diseases.name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome
cause: Not fully understood — linked to gut-brain signalling, food sensitivities, past gut infection, stress
symptoms: Abdominal pain linked to bowel habit changes
Diarrhoea, constipation, or an alternating pattern
remedies: Diagnosis by exclusion with a doctor
Dietary guidance such as a low-FODMAP trial under professional supervision
naturalRemedies: Peppermint tea or oil is commonly discussed for symptom relief

diseases.name: Type 2 Diabetes
cause: Excess body weight, especially visceral fat
remedies: Diagnosis and ongoing management by a doctor
Blood glucose monitoring
Medication as prescribed when needed
naturalRemedies: Cinnamon and high-fibre meals are commonly discussed as supportive of steadier blood sugar, alongside — not instead of — medical care

diseases.name: Chronic Kidney Disease
cause: Long-standing uncontrolled diabetes or hypertension (most common causes)
remedies: Regular kidney function monitoring by a doctor
Blood pressure and blood sugar control
Specialist (nephrology) care as the condition progresses
homeRemedies: Moderating sodium and protein per medical advice
naturalRemedies: Many "natural" supplements are hard on the kidneys — always check with a doctor before using any supplement alongside kidney disease

diseases.name: Urinary Tract Infection
cause: Bacteria entering the urinary tract, most often E. coli
remedies: Diagnosis via urine test and antibiotics as prescribed by a doctor
naturalRemedies: Cranberry products are commonly discussed for prevention, though evidence is mixed — they do not replace antibiotics for an active infection

diseases.name: Migraine
cause: Not fully understood — involves nerve and blood-vessel changes in the brain
Triggers include stress, certain foods, hormonal shifts, poor sleep
remedies: Diagnosis and a management plan from a doctor
Prescribed medication for acute attacks or prevention when frequent
naturalRemedies: Magnesium-rich foods and consistent caffeine intake (avoiding sudden changes) are commonly discussed as supportive

diseases.name: Sciatica
cause: Compression or irritation of the sciatic nerve, often from a herniated disc or spinal narrowing
symptoms: Pain radiating from the lower back through the hip and down one leg
remedies: Diagnosis and imaging if needed from a doctor
Physical therapy
Medication or, rarely, surgery for severe or persistent cases
homeRemedies: Gentle stretching and movement as tolerated
naturalRemedies: Gentle yoga stretches are commonly used alongside medical guidance

diseases.name: Osteoporosis
cause: Low calcium/vitamin D intake over many years
symptoms: Often silent until a fracture occurs
remedies: Bone density screening (DEXA scan) as advised by a doctor
Medication when prescribed for higher-risk cases
homeRemedies: Adequate calcium and vitamin D intake
naturalRemedies: Sensible sun exposure supports natural vitamin D production

diseases.name: Sarcopenia
cause: Age-related muscle loss, accelerated by inactivity and inadequate protein intake
remedies: Assessment by a doctor or physiotherapist
homeRemedies: Resistance/strength training, even at low intensity, most weeks
naturalRemedies: No single herbal remedy is well-established; consistent activity and protein intake are the best-supported approaches

diseases.name: Hypothyroidism
cause: Autoimmune thyroiditis (Hashimoto's) — the most common cause
remedies: Blood testing and diagnosis by a doctor
Thyroid hormone replacement as prescribed, with regular monitoring
homeRemedies: Consistent, adequate iodine intake without excess
naturalRemedies: Thyroid hormone medication should never be replaced with supplements — check any supplement with a doctor first

diseases.name: Eczema (Atopic Dermatitis)
cause: Skin barrier dysfunction combined with an overactive immune response
Triggers include irritants, allergens, dry weather, stress
symptoms: Itchy, dry, inflamed patches of skin
remedies: Diagnosis and a treatment plan from a doctor or dermatologist
Prescribed topical treatment for flare-ups when needed
homeRemedies: Avoiding known triggers and harsh soaps
naturalRemedies: Oatmeal baths are commonly used to soothe irritated skin

diseases.name: Cataracts
cause: Age-related clouding of the eye's lens
symptoms: Increased glare sensitivity, especially at night
remedies: Regular eye exams for diagnosis and monitoring
Surgical lens replacement when vision is significantly affected — highly effective and common
naturalRemedies: Antioxidant-rich foods (leafy greens, citrus) are commonly discussed as supportive of eye health generally

lifestyles.name: Regular Physical Activity
activities: 150 min/week moderate aerobic activity, or 75 min vigorous
Strength/resistance training 2x/week
Daily movement breaks if desk-based
food: Balanced meals with adequate protein to support recovery
avoid: Prolonged sitting for many hours without breaks
Overtraining without adequate rest

lifestyles.name: Balanced Nutrition
activities: Planning meals around vegetables, whole grains and varied protein sources
Cooking at home most days
food: A variety of vegetables and fruit daily
avoid: Excess added sugar
Excess sodium
Highly processed food as a regular staple

lifestyles.name: Quality Sleep
activities: Consistent sleep and wake times, even on weekends
A wind-down routine before bed
7–9 hours nightly for most adults
food: Limiting caffeine in the afternoon and evening
avoid: Screens immediately before bed
Large meals or alcohol close to bedtime
Irregular sleep schedules

lifestyles.name: Stress Management
activities: Regular relaxation practice (breathing exercises, meditation, prayer or reflection)
Time in nature
Maintaining adequate social support
food: Regular, balanced meals rather than skipping under stress
avoid: Chronic overwork without recovery time
Using alcohol or excess food as the main coping strategy

lifestyles.name: Hydration
activities: Drinking water steadily through the day rather than all at once
Increasing intake with heat, activity or illness
avoid: Relying on sugary drinks for hydration
Excess caffeine or alcohol, which increase fluid loss

lifestyles.name: Avoiding Tobacco & Limiting Alcohol
activities: Seeking support to quit smoking or vaping where relevant
Setting personal limits on alcohol intake
food: Not applicable — this habit is about substance avoidance rather than food
avoid: Smoking or vaping
Excess alcohol intake

lifestyles.name: Preventive Health Screenings
activities: Routine blood pressure and blood sugar checks
Age-appropriate screenings (cholesterol, bone density, cancer screening etc.) as advised by a doctor
food: Not applicable — this habit is about routine check-ups
avoid: Ignoring persistent symptoms
Skipping recommended check-ups for years at a time

lifestyles.name: Social Connection & Mental Wellbeing
activities: Maintaining regular contact with family and friends
Participating in community or faith activities
Seeking support (professional or personal) when struggling
food: Shared meals as a way to connect
avoid: Prolonged isolation
Ignoring ongoing low mood or anxiety without seeking support

lifestyles.name: Sun-Smart Habits
activities: Sensible, protected sun exposure for vitamin D
Wearing sunglasses and sunscreen during prolonged exposure
food: Vitamin D-supporting foods (fatty fish, fortified foods), especially with limited sun
avoid: Prolonged unprotected sun exposure
Complete sun avoidance without another vitamin D source

lifestyles.name: Posture & Ergonomics
activities: Setting up a supportive desk and chair height
Regular movement breaks every 30–60 minutes
Core and back-strengthening exercise
food: Adequate calcium and vitamin D for bone and spine support
avoid: Long unbroken periods of sitting or screen use
Slouched or unsupported posture for extended periods

ages.name: Infant
notes: Breast milk or formula is the primary source of nutrition for the first 6 months
Higher proportion of calories from fat than any other life stage
Solid foods and iron-rich foods typically introduced around 6 months
Small, frequent feeds; rapid growth drives high nutrient needs per kg body weight

ages.name: Child
notes: Steady growth requires reliable calcium, iron and protein intake
Establishing food habits and variety matters as much as any single nutrient
Portion sizes scale with age, not adult-sized servings

ages.name: Adolescent
notes: Growth-spurt years raise calorie, calcium and iron needs
Iron needs rise further for menstruating teens
Peak bone-building window — calcium and vitamin D matter most here

ages.name: Adult
notes: Focus shifts to maintenance: balanced macronutrients and fibre for heart and digestive health
Activity level is the main driver of energy needs
Good window to build habits that protect later decades

ages.name: Midlife Adult
notes: Bone density needs closer attention — calcium and vitamin D intake matters more
Metabolic rate typically slows, so portion and sodium/fat awareness increases
Heart-health nutrition (fibre, potassium, limiting sodium) becomes more protective

ages.name: Older Adult
notes: Protein needs rise per kg body weight to help offset age-related muscle loss
Vitamin B12 absorption typically declines, raising the value of B12-rich or fortified foods
Thirst sensation weakens, so hydration needs conscious attention
Smaller, more nutrient-dense meals are often more realistic than large meals
